reason: The text demonstrates agency exercised by non-leaders. Jehosheba, a royal princess but not a political leader, independently takes heroic action—she steals away the young prince Joash and hides him in the temple for six years, risking her own safety. Additionally, the common people (עַם הָאָ֙רֶץ) display agency by actively destroying the temple of Baal, smashing altars and images (וַֽיִּתְּצֻ֗הוּ אֶת־ מִזְבְּחוֹתָיו וְאֶת־ צְלָמָיו֙ שִׁבְּר֣וּ הֵיטֵ֔ב), and rejoicing over the new king (וַיִּשְׂמַ֥ח כָּל־ עַם־ הָאָ֖רֶץ). While Jehoiada the priest organizes the coup, the people are not passive subjects but active participants in religious and political change.
